{{short description|German biologist}}
'''Ilka Reinhardt''' (born 1966 in the [[German Democratic Republic|GDR]]) is a German [[biologist]] and [[wolf]] expert.<ref>''[http://www.canidensymposium-berlin.de/referent/ilka-reinhardt-2/ Ilka Reinhardt - Biolgraphy]''</ref> She is together with [[Gesa Kluth]] Founder and director of [[LUPUS - Institute for Wolf Monitoring and Research in Germany]]<ref>ResearchGate: ''[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gesa_Kluth Gesa Kluth LUPUS German Institute for Wolf Monitoring and Research]''</ref> and the Freundeskreis freilebender Wölfe.<ref>Uwe Menschner, Andrea Hilscher: ''[https://www.lr-online.de/nachrichten/die-rundschau-zu-gast-bei-ilka-reinhardt-und-gesa-kluthspurensuche-in-der-lausitz_aid-3982526 The Rundschau as a guest of Ilka Reinhardt and Gesa Kluth - Spurensuche in der Lausitz].'' In: ''[[Lausitzer Rundschau]].'' 29 January 2008</ref><ref>Circle of Friends of Wild Wolves: ''[https://www.freundeskreiswoelfe.de/verein The foundation of the association]''</ref> She was appointed by the Saxon State Ministry for the Environment and Agriculture as the wolf commissioner. Ilka Reinhardt works with the [[International Fund for Animal Welfare]] (IFAW) and [[Naturschutzbund Deutschland]]. In [[Poland]], the biologist [[Sabina Nowak]] has a similar position. Ilka Reinhardt and Sabina Nowak are members of the [[Large Carnivore Initiative for Europe]]<ref>Large Carnivore Initiative for Europe: ''[https://www.lcie.org/About-LCIE/-Who-are-we Who we are - Members of the LCIE specialist group]''</ref> and cooperate with the CEWolf Consortium.<ref>Senckenberg: ''[https://www.senckenberg.de/de/institute/senckenberg-gesellschaft-fuer-naturforschung-frankfurt-main/abt-fliessgewaesseroekologie-und-naturschutzforschung/das-cewolf-konsortium/ The CEwolf Consortium ]''</ref>

== Career ==
Growing up in [[Potsdam]] and [[Berlin]], she first completed an apprenticeship as skilled worker for animal production. After the [[German reunification]] she studied biology and found her main interest in [[wildlife biology]]. She was involved in a bear project in [[Slovenia]] and worked on [[badger]]s in [[Switzerland]]. The topic of her diploma thesis is [[Eurasian lynx|lynx]] occurrences in Slovenia. After her diploma she met Gesa Kluth in Berlin, with whom she founded the ''Wildbiologisches Büro LUPUS'' in Spreewitz in 2003.<ref>''[http://www.naturmagazin.info/ausgaben/2-2017/titelthema/kRAS4WvJwu/ The wolf expert] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208124455/http://www.naturmagazin.info/ausgaben/2-2017/titelthema/kRAS4WvJwu/ |date=2018-02-08 }}.'' In: ''Naturmagazin Berlin-Brandenburg.'' 2/2017</ref><ref>''[http://www.lausitz-wolf.de/index.php?id=874 Wildlife Biology Bureau Lupus].'' lausitz-wolf.de</ref><ref>[[Sachsen Anhalt]] Landeseamt für Umweltschutz, Wildbiologisches Büro LUPUS, Bundesforstbetrieb Nördliches Sachsen-Anhalt: ''[https://lau.sachsen-anhalt.de/fileadmin/Bibliothek/Politik_und_Verwaltung/MLU/LAU/Naturschutz/Grossraubtiere-Wolf/Dateien/Projektinformation_1.pdf Untersuchung des Raum-Zeit-Verhaltens von Wölfen in Sachsen-Anhalt unter Einbeziehung eventueller Abwanderung von Jungwölfen mit Hilfe von GPS-GSM-Telemetrie] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231212083351/https://lau.sachsen-anhalt.de/fileadmin/Bibliothek/Politik_und_Verwaltung/MLU/LAU/Naturschutz/Grossraubtiere-Wolf/Dateien/Projektinformation_1.pdf |date=2023-12-12 }}''</ref> Like [[Sabina Nowak]], Ilka Reinhardt became a member of the Large Carnivore Initiative for Europe (LCIE) under the chair [[Luigi Boitani]]. Together with Gesa Kluth, she supervised and promoted the re-immigration of wolves to Germany in accordance with his instructions. On behalf of the [[Federal Agency for Nature Conservation|Bundesamt für Naturschutz]], the two women played a key role in the development of the Standards for wolf monitoring for Germany. They conduct wolf monitoring training courses for interested parties from Germany and neighbouring countries.<ref>Wolfcenter Dörverden: ''[https://www.wolfcenter.de/2013/10/02/pressemitteilung-ein-grosser-erfolg-das-1-internationales-wolfsymposium-des-wolfcenter-doerverden-zeigte-optionen-auf-fuer-ein-gemeinsames-leben-mit-dem-wolf/ 1. Internationales Wolfssymposium]'' 2013</ref>

== Lectures ==

In 2013 Ilka Reinhardt spoke as a speaker at the International Wolf Symposium at the Wolfcenter in [[Dörverden]].<ref>Wolfcenter Dörverden: [https://www.wolfcenter.de/2013/10/02/pressemitteilung-ein-grosser-erfolg-das-1-internationales-wolfsymposium-des-wolfcenter-doerverden-zeigte-optionen-auf-fuer-ein-gemeinsames-leben-mit-dem-wolf/ ''1. Internationales Wolfssymposium''] 2013</ref>

As a speaker at the [[Naturschutzbund Deutschland|NABU]] Wolf Conference 2015, she provided information on the conservation status of the wolf, population development and monitoring: "There is a constant debate about whether the wolf should be listed in Annex IV or V of the Habitats Directive. Founding countries of the EU have classified him in IV. That was easy, because these countries were virtually wolf-free. Countries that joined the EU later negotiated its inclusion in Annex V precisely because wolves were already present there. Animals are protected in Annex V, but legal hunting can be carried out under certain conditions. For example, wolves are hunted as an Annex V species in the Baltic States, but not in Poland. How the protection status is filled in is a matter for the country concerned" (Quote Ilka Reinhard).<ref>'' [https://www.jagdverband.de/content/nabu-wolfskonferenz NABU Wolf Conference 2015].'' jagdverband.de, 1 October 2015,  (Ilka Reinhardt).</ref><ref>European Commission: [http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/species/carnivores/pdf/task_1_part1_statusoflcineurope.pdf ''Status, management and distribution of large carnivores – bear, lynx, wolf & wolverine – in Europe December 2012.''] page 50.</ref>
